client_brief:
Verranza Coastal Retreats: In villa season card run

Project overview
Verranza Coastal Retreats is the repeat client for this benchmark series. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into In villa season card run, twelve records and Verranza collection photography.

What we will provide
verranza_captures/ (21 frames across three villas, 6720 x 4480); verranza_season_card.pdf; verranza_rates.csv; verranza_amenities.txt; verranza_owner_note.png; verranza_welcome_stills/ (6 still life frames, 6720 x 4480); verranza_cove_mark.png. Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Scope and deliverables
- In villa season card run, twelve records: Twelve cards, one villa and season per page, at the card's true trim, built from the printer's own artwork rather than a redrawn approximation: each carrying its own villa's finished photograph bound per record, its own rate, its own minimum stay written...
- Verranza collection photography: The full three villa set brought to one collection target: one white point, one black point, one treatment of stone and shadow, one relationship between interior and exterior brightness, with water that could exist at that hour and no fake high dynamic...

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$3,000-$7,000 fixed; target delivery 2 to 4 weeks; one direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Anchor: the Upwork real estate finishing brief quoted in the ledger, posted by a boutique vacation rental manager asking for a consistent premium visual identity across the whole portfolio with a natural, realistic look, and carrying an explicit do not want list: no fake high dynamic range, no over saturation, no unrealistically blue pools. That post named no company, place or vendor, so the collection is laundered to the fictional Verranza Coastal Retreats on the fictional cove of Anse Verranza on the southern French coast, with the invented villas Solane, Cascina and Aubine. This is a REBUILD rather than a strengthen. The killed original ran three independent short imaging passes and finished there, which is a finishing job rather than a commission and sat on one surface. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller version is, because the finishing pass is only the front half of what this client actually needs: HTML authoring now produces a native editable multi root document at mixed canvas sizes, so the presentation and the booking pages are real deliverables, and a bare press PDF from their printer can be reverse engineered into a live merge template, so the twelve in villa season cards become a genuine record per page run whose photographs are the very frames the finishing pass produced. That dependency, a badly finished frame being invisible until it lands in the card at the card's crop, is what turns three separate passes into one engagement. The same capabilities change the imaging half too: the collection's only graphic mark, a hand inked cove motif that survives as a scan and as an etch on one villa's door glass, can be recovered as real vector rather than redrawn, and the contractual welcome provision the client leaves in every house can be isolated onto the collection's own ground, so the raster surface is a full imaging engagement rather than a grade and crop pass.

price_band_and_audience: Villas at 1,800 to 4,200 dollars a night, guests 40 to 65 booking whole property stays for a milestone, comparing the collection against hotels rather than against other rentals. The band is load bearing. At this price the grammar is generous negative space, full bleed architecture allowed to be quiet, rates carried in a discreet table rather than announced, and photography that is believable before it is impressive, because the guest who pays 4,200 a night has been to the actual house and will recognise a lie in the water. Push it down into a bargain rental grid of eight thumbnails, a price badge and a book now block and the collection reads as an aggregator listing and the rate stops being defensible. Push it further up into pure sparseness with the rates hidden entirely and a travel agency cannot sell from it. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even with every technical gate green. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 4,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: The whole house, the whole coast.
brand_identity.sector: Boutique luxury vacation-rental collection managing whole-property villas on the southern French coast.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Liguria, Italy; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Verranza Coastal Retreats is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is Liguria, Italy, and this commission covers phase 2: booking collateral and in-villa season cards.
brand_identity.audience: Guests aged 40 to 65 booking a whole villa for a birthday, an anniversary or a multi-generation gathering, plus the travel agencies and private clients who book on their behalf. They have stayed in the real houses and will recognise anything that is not true.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Villas run 1,800 to 4,200 dollars a night depending on season, positioned against boutique hotels rather than other rentals. The grammar is generous space and quiet architecture, with rates carried in a discreet table rather than announced, so the collection never reads as an aggregator listing.
brand_identity.typography: One quiet prestige system: an elegant high-contrast serif for display and villa names, set with air, paired with a clean humanist sans for amenity tables, the rate ladder and body. Restraint over flourish, so it reads considered without tipping into fashion-house coldness a family will not book from.
brand_identity.voice: Calm, warm, understated. Describes what the house actually is at that hour, never oversells. Example line: "Warm stone, a long terrace, and the pool in real afternoon light."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The collection has a printed in-villa season card whose artwork is held by its printer as a press PDF, and a written owner note recording what the previous editor got wrong. There is no lost wordmark here; the constraint is photographic consistency across three villas shot on two trips by two people, with the second batch already worked on by an editor no longer used. The collection's one graphic mark is a small hand inked cove motif an artist drew for the founders, which survives only as a flatbed scan of the original inking and as the mark etched on Maison Aubine's door glass; it has never been redrawn or digitised, and the foil printer and the glass etcher need it as vector artwork. The contractual welcome provision left in every house exists only as a short still life set the manager shot on a villa's limestone counter.
brand_identity.values: Believable before impressive. One collection, not three holidays. Natural light, real shadow, honest water, and no fake high dynamic range or dyed pools.

assets_supplied.name: verranza_captures/ (21 frames across three villas, 6720 x 4480)
assets_supplied.kind: Architectural and interior capture of all three villas, gathered on two trips a year apart by two different photographers, delivered as a single folder with villa prefixes.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything we have for the three houses. The second trip came back already worked on by an editor we no longer use."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The second trip's frames arrived with a finishing curve already baked in, so they carry contrast that fights a global correction and their pool water already sits near the ceiling of its channel, which is precisely the look the manager rules out and which a moderate move cannot walk all the way back. Separately two of the twenty one are the same terrace from one tripod position a minute apart, so one villa reaches the presentation a frame short of what the folder count suggests.

assets_supplied.name: verranza_season_card.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The collection's existing in villa season card exactly as its printer holds it: a real press PDF, one card per page, a photograph panel at the top and then the season name, the nightly rate, the minimum stay and a short season note set as printed type.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our printer's file. We just want each villa and each season dropped into it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The season note frame on the printed sheet was sized to the shortest specimen the printer happened to set, and it is a fixed frame: a merged record longer than that does not spill and does not reflow, it simply stops rendering at the frame edge, so the page returns successfully with the sentence cut off at trim. The printed face also reads as separate blocks that the conversion does not necessarily expose as separate frames.

assets_supplied.name: verranza_rates.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Twelve rows: villa, season, nightly rate, minimum stay, and the season note that goes on the card, plus a column naming the villa photograph for each row.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Rates as they stand for the coming year. Twelve cards, three villas by four seasons."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One villa's shoulder season note runs two lines longer than every other record, and the minimum stay column is written three different ways across the twelve rows. Neither is visible from the file's shape, and the photograph column names only three distinct files for twelve rows.

assets_supplied.name: verranza_amenities.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the per villa amenity list, bed and bath counts, sleeping capacity, the included services, and the four season definitions with their date ranges.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What goes in the amenity table on each villa's page. The included services list is contractual."

assets_supplied.name: verranza_owner_note.png
assets_supplied.kind: Screengrab of the manager's own written note to the previous editor, listing what went wrong last time.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What we told the last person. Please read it before you start."

assets_supplied.name: verranza_welcome_stills/ (6 still life frames, 6720 x 4480)
assets_supplied.kind: A short still life set the manager shot of the welcome provision that is contractual with every whole house stay: the local rose, a boule of village bread, a jar of the estate olive oil, a bowl of figs and a folded linen bundle, each photographed on the warm limestone of a villa counter for the what is included section.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The welcome things we leave in every house, shot on the kitchen stone. We want them cut out clean on our own paper colour for the included page, not another room shot."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The rose, the clear glass, the pale crust and the honey oil all sit within a hair of the warm limestone they are shot on, so a one call subject knockout returns a clean looking complete cutout that has quietly bitten the pale glass shoulder or the crust edge where object and stone share value, and the bite is invisible until the cutout is placed on the Linen brand ground rather than on white. The bowl of figs, being dark, knocks out cleanly, so the route is a per frame decision rather than a global one, and two of the six are the same bottle from one position so the set lands one distinct object short of its count.

assets_supplied.name: verranza_cove_mark.png
assets_supplied.kind: A flatbed scan of the collection's only graphic mark: a small hand inked line drawing of the Anse Verranza cove, a stylised headland, the cove mouth and a single villa roofline, drawn for the founders by a local artist. Supplied as a high contrast scan of the original inking on off white paper; there is no vector version anywhere.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The little cove drawing from when we opened. It is etched on Maison Aubine's door glass and stamped on the card, and the vendors want a proper file. This scan is all we have."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The inked strokes carry hairline tapers and small enclosed counters, the cove mouth and the roofline's window openings, that a trace holds at full scan size and closes at the height the mark is actually reproduced, a thumbnail across the corner of the card and smaller again on the etched door glass. The aged ink and the warm off white paper run close in value across one edge of the sheet, so a selection naming the drawing rather than the ink returns the paper with it, and the scan is only modest resolution so the mark cannot be enlarged to buy back detail.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the cut edge survives where a pale object meets the warm stone it is sitting on. The welcome things are shot on a villa's limestone, and on some frames the rose, the clear glass shoulder or the pale crust sit at almost the value of the stone. The knockout reports success, the returned cutout is complete and clean at thumbnail scale, and the bite only exists along the short stretch where the pale object and the stone share luminance. Which frames it happens to is a property of each frame's own light and the object's own colour, not of the object, and there is no confidence figure and no edge report anywhere in the response.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not dodge it, because the edge quality is a fact about this frame meeting this tool and exists only after the call has run and the result is looked at on the ground it will sit on, the Linen brand ground, not on white. Nothing states it: the brief says only that the welcome things were shot on the kitchen stone. And it is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different chain for the affected frames, a material named selection of the limestone, inverted and filled to the brand ground.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re plan the knockout route per frame, re derive the affected cutouts through the selection and fill chain, and re inspect every cutout against the Linen brand ground rather than against white.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A what is included panel and a season social set in which the welcome objects have a chewed edge along the glass or the crust on the frames nobody looked at closely, on a collection whose whole pitch is that nothing is a little bit wrong.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered cove mark is still the mark at the height it actually reproduces. The trace comes back looking correct: the headland and the cove and the roofline are there, the counters are open, and at full scan scale on a white page it is a faithful recovery. The foil printer stamps it across the corner of the card at roughly a thumbnail, and the glass etcher puts it on Maison Aubine's door at hand small, and at those heights the hairline tapers fill in and the cove mouth and the window openings close into solid blobs. The tracer takes no options at all, so nothing about the trace call can be tuned; the only evidence is placing the artwork at its real reproduction size on its real ground and looking.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the answer depends on the trace, the reproduction height and the ground colour being present together, and the first two are produced by the agent while the third is a property of the card stock and the glass. Nothing states it: the brief asks for a proper file the vendors can use and says the mark has to still look drawn by hand. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different raster preparation feeding the same tracer, a differently worded ink level selection, a fill and flatten plate instead of a binary mask, or a bounds crop that changes what the tracer sees, since the tracer itself has no lever.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re prepare the raster on a different route, re trace, re inject the viewBox and strip the opaque ground path again, then re place the result at reproduction height on the card stock and on the glass colour and re judge, and state a safe minimum height in the handover once one is actually known.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The founders' mark foil stamped on the card and etched on the door glass as a row of solid blobs, on the one mark the collection has and on pieces a guest paying 4,200 a night holds and walks through.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the licensed frame belongs to this collection. The search returns only a small CDN thumbnail, so the frame's true white balance, its own baked contrast, how its horizon sits and how its water reads all exist only after the licence is taken and the full resolution file is pulled down. Even then the question is not whether the frame is good, it is whether it sits with these three specific villas at their finished target, which cannot be answered until the two are finally adjacent on the opening root. Every step up to that point returns success: the search succeeded, the licence succeeded, the download succeeded, and the thumbnail looked right.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not avoid it, because the only order that would is licensing several candidates and comparing them at full resolution, which spends licences on a guess. Nothing states it: the brief never mentions a bought frame at all, it simply asks for a collection presentation, and the do not want list is the client's art direction rather than a warning about stock. And the response is not a re run, it is a decision between grading the licensed frame to the collection target, taking a second licence on a different candidate, and restructuring the opening root around a villa frame instead, each of which changes what the presentation opens on and therefore what the social end card carries.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re grade or re license, and if neither brings the frame inside the collection, re plan the opening root and the social end card around villa photography and re cut those crops.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A presentation whose first screen is visibly a bought photograph next to three carefully finished houses, shown to a travel agency by a collection whose whole pitch is consistency.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work, which need authored fixed canvas documents, and which need a record per page run, given that only one surface here does each.
Which frames arrived already finished, and the fact that those need walking back rather than pushing further, which is the opposite move from the rest of the set.
Where restraint stops being restraint and becomes a flat picture, on a set whose client has an explicit written list of what not to do.
Selection prompt wording throughout: naming the terrace or the villa takes the place, naming the material's own colour, surface and form takes the material.
Knockout route per welcome still life, between the one call subject knockout and a material named selection of the warm limestone inverted and filled, where a pale object and pale stone share value.
Selection wording on the cove mark scan: naming the paper takes the substrate, naming the ink's own visual properties takes the mark.

Whether the single colour stamping version or the colour accurate variant is what the foil printer and the glass etcher actually need, judged at foil stamp height on the card and etch height on the door glass rather than at full scan scale.
Whether the printer's card converts to separated frames or one continuous flow, and therefore whether the mapping is per frame or offset based inside one story.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of a beautiful villa. IDENTITY: these are three specific houses that guests will physically arrive at, and a regenerated pool, terrace or view is a misrepresentation the manager can be held to, which is precisely why the do not want list exists and why they have lost bookings before. SPEC: twelve cards at the printer's trim, one villa and season per page, each field present in full, plus crops at fixed destinations with nothing enlarged, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: rates change twice a year and the client explicitly cannot re commission, so a flat render is worth nothing to them. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: is this water believable, does this bought frame belong here, does this note fit the frame, did the type survive the import on the roots nobody can preview, did this cutout bite the pale glass against the stone, does this trace still read as the founders' mark at foil stamp height. And the cove mark is a specific hand inked drawing that has to be RECOVERED rather than reinvented, because a regenerated mark is a different drawing in a different hand that the foil printer and the glass etcher cannot cut from a picture, while the welcome objects are the villa's own things isolated onto the collection's own ground, not stock still lifes.
